summary: notification-service is being OOMKilled by an unbounded in-memory template cache (TemplateCache, ConcurrentHashMap keyed by template+locale+userSegment) introduced by deployment dep-5402 (v3.8.0) on 2026-03-21T00:00:14Z. The cache grows with zero evictions (evictions=0; 9000 entries -> 18000 entries in one hour; 188100 entries at the peak), and memory_pct climbs in a linear sawtooth from ~48% to ~98% before each restart — a stable ~24h cycle producing restarts at Mar 21 22:00, Mar 22 22:00 and Mar 23 20:00 (the third restart, exit code 137 at 19:59:21Z). CPU (~25%), request_rate (~140 req/s) and latency (~110ms) are all flat, ruling out load/capacity causes. The reported Kafka maintenance (cfg-2410, retention reduction at 18:00 Mar 23) is coincidental: the identical OOM cycle occurred on Mar 21 and Mar 22 with no config change, kafka shows 0 under-replicated partitions and no rebalance/error logs, and consumer_lag only spikes during the restart windows (lag is a consequence of the consumer being down, not the trigger). Root cause: bad deployment (unbounded cache) in notification-service.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Unbounded in-memory TemplateCache introduced by dep-5402 leaks heap until OOM
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Deploy dep-5402 (v3.8.0) added an in-memory ConcurrentHashMap template cache with no eviction. Under steady traffic the cache grows without bound (~9000 entries/hour, evictions=0), linearly consuming heap (old gen) until the container hits its memory limit and is OOMKilled, restarting ~every 24h. The reported Kafka replay/lag is a downstream symptom of the restart, not the cause.

causal_chain.claim: dep-5402 deploys in-memory template cache without eviction
Heap memory climbs linearly from ~48% to ~98% and resets on restart (24h sawtooth)
Container OOMKilled (exit 137), restart count increments once per cycle
Consumer lag spikes only during restart windows; kafka broker itself healthy

assumptions: The cache is not bounded by any TTL/size config elsewhere (evictions=0 in logs supports this)
~9000 entries/hour at steady ~140 req/s is consistent with the observed memory slope

ranked_hypotheses.title: Kafka maintenance (cfg-2410 retention change) triggered a replay that overran the consumer
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The Kafka maintenance at 2026-03-23T18:00Z that reduced log.retention.ms drove a consumer replay/rebalance, spiking lag and causing notification-service to choke and OOM.

causal_chain.claim: kafka retention reduced to 3 days at 18:00

assumptions: A retention reduction could force a replay
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Memory climb and OOM restarts began on 2026-03-21, two days before the 18:00 Mar 23 Kafka change; the same ~24h sawtooth repeats on Mar 21 and Mar 22 with no config change. kafka shows 0 under-replicated partitions and no rebalance/error logs during the maintenance window, and a retention reduction (deleting old segments) does not cause consumers to re-read data.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Consumer replay/lag is the primary fault with no faulty change
ranked_hypotheses.statement: notification-service is simply overwhelmed by message volume/replay, saturating memory via in-flight buffering; lag is the cause rather than a symptom.

causal_chain.claim: message volume causes lag and memory pressure

assumptions: Lag could buffer unboundedly in memory
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: request_rate, CPU and latency are all flat; memory consumption tracks cache entry count not message rate; kafka message rate is steady ~2400/s; lag spikes only during restart windows.

facts.statement: notification-service memory was flat ~48% pre-deploy and began a linear climb from Mar 21 02:00 onward.
Memory follows a ~24h sawtooth resetting on restart, matching OOM restarts rather than load.
Restart count went 0 -> 1 -> 2 -> 3 at Mar 21 22:00, Mar 22 22:00, Mar 23 20:00 — one per cycle.
An OOMKilled (exit code 137) event was logged at 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z.
TemplateCache logs show evictions=0 with size growing 9000->18000 entries/hour and 188100 at peak.
dep-5402 (v3.8.0) added an in-memory template cache and rolled out at 2026-03-21T00:00:14Z.
First GC-pause warning appeared 2026-03-21T03:00:44Z, ~3h after dep-5402 rollout.
CPU stayed flat ~25% with no rise during the memory climb.
request_rate stayed flat ~140 req/s across the window.
latency_p99 stayed flat ~110ms across the window.
The only config change was kafka log.retention.ms reduced to 3 days at 18:00 Mar 23.
kafka had 0 under-replicated partitions and steady ~2400 msg/s intake.
notification-service consumer_lag spikes coincide with restart windows.
kafka logs during maintenance show only a benign TLS-cipher warning, no rebalance/errors.
No deployments occurred on any service after 2026-03-23T16:00Z.

assumptions: The template cache has no TTL/size cap configured elsewhere; evictions=0 in logs strongly supports this.
The ~9000 entries/hour growth rate is consistent with the steady request rate and the observed ~1.5-2%/hour memory slope.
The 48%->98% memory cycle is heap/anonymous memory growth from the cache rather than native/off-heap leaks not visible in cache stats.

timeline.event: Baseline: memory_pct flat ~48%, restarts=0, CPU ~25%, stable.
Deployment dep-5402 (v3.8.0) 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering' rollout complete.
memory_pct begins steady linear climb (~52.7% and rising).
First GC-pause warning: 'GC pause 253ms exceeded 200ms target'.
First OOM restart (restarts=1); memory resets to ~48%; consumer_lag spikes to avg 2273.
Second OOM restart (restarts=2); memory resets; consumer_lag spikes (avg 790).
Kafka maintenance cfg-2410: log.retention.ms reduced to 3 days.
restarts=3; memory resets to ~48%; consumer_lag spikes (avg 1542); emails delayed ~25 min.
Post-restart TemplateCache stats: size=9000 entries, evictions=0 (cache refilling immediately).
TemplateCache stats: size=18000 entries, evictions=0 — linear unbounded growth continues.

recommended_actions.action: Roll back notification-service to the pre-dep-5402 version (or disable the TemplateCache code path), then confirm the memory sawtooth disappears.
recommended_actions.rationale: The memory climb maps exactly to the unbounded TemplateCache introduced by dep-5402; rollback removes the leaking component and restores the flat ~48% baseline.

recommended_actions.action: Add a bounded cache (maximumSize/TTL, e.g. Caffeine with eviction) to the template cache and emit eviction metrics.
recommended_actions.rationale: The root cause is an unbounded map; a size/TTL cap with eviction prevents unbounded heap growth.

recommended_actions.action: Add an alert on old-gen heap trend / restarts and on TemplateCache entry count so growth is caught before OOM.
recommended_actions.rationale: The leak ran for 24h before each OOM; a heap-growth alert would have caught it on Mar 21.

recommended_actions.action: Treat the Kafka maintenance theory as a red herring; do not pursue a replay/throttling remediation for this incident.
recommended_actions.rationale: Identical OOM cycles predate the kafka change and kafka was healthy (0 under-replicated partitions, no rebalance logs); lag only spikes during restarts.

data_gaps: No heap-dump / per-object memory allocation breakdown to confirm the TemplateCache is the dominant heap consumer (inferred from cache stats + timing, not directly measured).
TemplateCache logs appear only on Mar 23; cache-size history for Mar 21-22 is not available to directly tie entry count to the earlier climbs.
No email-provider telemetry (external node has has_telemetry=false), so its contribution to email delays cannot be assessed.

findings.statement: notification-service memory_pct was flat at ~48% through 2026-03-20 (pre-deploy), then began a steady linear climb from 2026-03-21T02:00Z (~52.7%) onward.

notification-service memory shows a repeating ~24h sawtooth: climbing to ~98% then resetting to ~48% (resets at Mar 21 22:00, Mar 22 22:00, Mar 23 20:00), consistent with OOM restarts, not a load spike.
notification-service restarts were 0 for the entire pre-deploy day, then incremented to 1 (Mar 21 22:00), 2 (Mar 22 22:00) and 3 (Mar 23 20:00) — one restart per ~24h.
notification-service OOMKilled with exit code 137 was logged at 2026-03-23T19:59:21Z.

TemplateCache stats show an unbounded cache with zero evictions: size=188100 entries, evictions=0 at 18:54; after restart size=9000 entries, evictions=0 at 21:00; then size=18000 entries, evictions=0 at 22:00 — growing ~9000 entries/hour with no eviction.
Deployment dep-5402 (v3.8.0, 'Add in-memory template cache for email rendering', keyed by template+locale+userSegment) is live and completed rollout at 2026-03-21T00:00:14Z.

refs.quote: deployment dep-5402 (v3.8.0) rollout complete, all pods ready
Add in-memory template cache for email rendering

findings.statement: The memory climb began ~2h after dep-5402 rollout: first GC-pause warning 'GC pause 253ms exceeded 200ms target' at 2026-03-21T03:00:44Z, with repeated old-gen 'heap usage ... over 90 (old gen)' warnings from 18:34Z on Mar 23.

refs.quote: heap usage 5% over 90 (old gen), full GC took 4152ms

findings.statement: notification-service CPU was flat at ~25% throughout (min 21.78, max 28.5) with no rise during the memory climb, ruling out CPU saturation.
notification-service request_rate was flat ~140 req/s across the whole window (min 115.35, max 172.03) with no increase at onset, so the memory growth is not traffic-driven.
notification-service latency_p99 was flat ~110ms throughout (min 96.63, max 124.49), so latency did not degrade before the OOM.
The only config change in the window was cfg-2410 on kafka (log.retention.ms 604800000 -> 259200000, 'Kafka maintenance: reduce retention to 3 days') at 2026-03-23T18:00:00Z.

refs.quote: Kafka maintenance: reduce retention to 3 days

findings.statement: kafka showed 0 under-replicated partitions for every 30-min bucket from 16:00 to 23:30 on Mar 23, and its message intake rate was steady ~2400 msg/s across the window.

notification-service consumer_lag spikes (e.g. avg 2273 at Mar 21 22:00, avg 810 at Mar 23 18:00, avg 1542 at Mar 23 20:00) coincide with the restart windows, i.e. lag accumulates while the consumer is restarting, not before the fault.
kafka logs during the maintenance window show only one benign WARN ('deprecated TLS cipher offered by client'), with no rebalance/reassignment/error entries.

refs.quote: deprecated TLS cipher offered by client

findings.statement: No deployment occurred on any service between 2026-03-23T16:00Z and 23:59Z.
